record.paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant c such that every graph G admits a bisection (S, T) with |N_T(u)| >= d_S(u) - c for every u in S and |N_S(v)| >= d_T(v) - c for every v in T?

evidence.quote:
There is almost no progress on this conjecture as I know. Even a constant c is not known such that every graph G has a bisection S, S¯ with
|NS¯(u)| ≥ dS(u) − c for each u ∈ S,
and
|NS(v)| ≥ dS¯(v) − c for each v ∈ S. ¯

artifact.self_contained_problem: Does there exist an absolute constant $c \geq 0$ such that every finite simple graph $G=(V,E)$ admits a bisection, i.e., a partition $V = S \cup T$ with $\bigl||S|-|T|\bigr| \leq 1$, satisfying the following local degree condition: for every vertex $u \in S$, the number of neighbors of $u$ in $T$ is at least $d_S(u) - c$, and for every vertex $v \in T$, the number of neighbors of $v$ in $S$ is at least $d_T(v) - c$? Here $d_X(w)$ denotes the number of neighbors of $w$ lying in the set $X$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a constant-error weakening of the Bollobás–Scott bisection conjecture. Recent work (2025) on bisections of graphs under degree constraints describes the weaker version as "widely open" and proves only results obtaining roughly (1/4)d_G(v) in each side, leaving a factor-of-2 gap; no absolute constant c as required is known.

status_evidence.title: Bisections of graphs under degree constraints
status_evidence.snippet: its equally important weaker version...remains widely open
status_evidence.claim: The weaker (constant-error) version of the Bollobás–Scott bisection conjecture remains open; current results achieve only ~(1/4)d_G(v) bounds.

status_evidence.title: Bisections of graphs (Lee, Loh, Sudakov)
status_evidence.claim: Earlier work establishes related bisection results but does not yield a constant-error local bisection for all graphs.
